summary: Pre-merge review of the staged 2026-09-22 working tree - automatic host fencing slices 1 to 4c, the host hardware and sensor slices, the pool Hosts tab and Stats palette work, and the release-publishes-website workflow change - and the fixes it produced. Nothing in that work had been committed or built into a package or ISO. Twenty-three behavioural defects were fixed and recorded as BUG-0418 to BUG-0440 in docs/BUG_LEDGER.md, each with a regression check that was observed failing on the unfixed code and passing with the fix. Core: the pool cluster keeps its nodelist when a host is still without a peer origin, so a mid-rollout join no longer tears the cluster down; LeavePoolCluster releases the corosync.conf it owns, so Host fencing off then clustered storage works; the IPMI fence runs over RMCP+ with --lanplus and renders lanplus=1 in the CIB; a truncated fence-check pass merges instead of erasing; a peer-offered fence password goes through vmhost.FenceSecretUsable; the local BMC record names its credential in the same write as the slot and backs a refusing controller off for one check interval; an ejected membership row no longer holds a machine's SMBIOS identity; the master derives its peer origin from the listener it is configured with; promotion counts a watchdog proof, fences by the method readiness promised, and an armed master is boot-restricted after its own watchdog could have reset it; an armed host no longer reads its own sbd as a foreign holder of the watchdog. Hardware and sensors: hwmon reads are bounded and return the last completed values, the 24-sensor budget cuts by priority, an upgraded host at the 128-series cap admits a temperature, and virtual block devices are not reported as installed disks. Controller: moveRecordedMaster is scoped to the pool, so a master cannot hand its pool row to a host of another pool. Web: a refused Host fencing toggle goes to the panel action alert instead of the membership-read error, and chart series 2 to 5 meet the 3:1 non-text contrast minimum. Release: the website release id is left to the deploy script, and the credential check, Node setup and website build run before the tag moves. Documentation: the fencing QA page records that no physical hardware was involved, the guide pages and plans were corrected to the behaviour that is actually implemented, the CHANGELOG evidence banner was widened, and docs/API.md, docs/guide/usage-history.md and the two plans were corrected on the derived peer origin and the sensor budget. An independent review of the fixes then found one more reset path (BUG-0440: two hosts draining from a four-host pool during a teardown left the survivors inquorate), a bounded hwmon read that still waited its full bound when a read was already in flight and served a frozen reading for a dead sensor, and an IPv6 wildcard bind the derived peer origin did not recognise; all three were fixed with the same red-to-green regression checks.

guide.reason: Operator-visible behaviour and operator-facing statements changed. docs/guide/usage-history.md now says the CPU package and NVMe temperatures are kept ahead of individual disk temperatures when the 24-sensor limit bites, and that a sensor that stops answering costs one gap in its own chart rather than holding up the sampling. docs/guide/join-a-pool.md says the master records the address its pool-peer listener is bound to, with the default-route fallback described as the wildcard-bind case. docs/guide/pool-authority-and-recovery.md now states that a promotion works either through a fence device or through the old master's own armed watchdog, that a host excluded by its own watchdog is not powered off, that a restarted master is restricted when it has armed this pool's watchdog, and carries a Verification bullet stating plainly that the fencing work has no hardware evidence and the browser review used mocked replies. docs/guide/change-management-network.md gains the prerequisite that a host feeding a watchdog cannot take a staged management-network change, with both refusals quoted. docs/guide/host-maintenance-mode.md corrects the claim that maintenance mode is not part of any failure-recovery story and describes the teardown an operator sees. docs/guide/publish-a-release.md no longer asserts public clearance and says the website is built before the release is created. docs/guide/README.md's index line is corrected to name the armed-watchdog alternative.

api.reason: No endpoint, payload or capability shape changed, on either the Controller-to-Core or the client-facing side. Three Core refusal sentences on existing operations did: the join invitation gained "the pool master's peer listen address is not an address and port" for a malformed --pool-peer-listen value, the promotion fence step now refuses with "pool host <id> cannot be excluded: <readiness reason>" instead of a separate no-recorded-profile sentence, and "pool peer state is unavailable" is new on the promotion path when the host's own pool-peer record cannot be read. Every fix is internal to a host or to the Controller's own database writer. --lanplus and the cipher flag are argv of the fence agent the host runs and a property of the stonith resource it creates, neither of which crosses an API; the master deriving its peer origin from its configured pool-peer listener changes only the value behind the existing optional master_url, whose validation, default and refusal are unchanged; poolLocalBMCRecord.Ref and RetryAfter are private fields of the host's own pool-peer.json and default to zero on an existing record; the hwmon bound and the sensor priority change which host-local values fill the same fields, with HardwareMaxSensors, HardwareMaxDisks and the /hardware and /stats shapes untouched; the disk filter only removes entries that were never installed hardware; and the Controller's moveRecordedMaster scoping changes no response. docs/API.md is edited only to correct two sentences that described behaviour inaccurately - the derived peer origin and the sensor budget - so no reference area page is claimed as a contract update. python3 scripts/generate_api.py --check passes unchanged.

roadmap.reason: The published roadmap states shipped capability at a coarser grain than a pre-merge review pass. Nothing here adds or removes a capability; it corrects defects in work the roadmap does not yet claim, and the fencing and hardware plans keep their open gates explicit.

state.reason: Every durable record these fixes touch is host-owned and already replicates from the pool master, and nothing was added to the Controller. The Controller fix is the opposite: it stops a master's report from moving a pool row and its storage, network and media mirrors to a host of another pool, so the Controller's mirrors stay a projection of what the hosts report. Delete the Controller, install a fresh one and connect the pool masters, and the fence profiles, provisioned accounts, machine identities, armed reports, peer origins and boot restrictions all come back from the hosts; no operator re-enters anything and no workload stops.
state.record: On each host, in its own pool-peer.json: poolLocalBMCRecord gains Ref, the reference to the fence credential the account's password is written under, saved with the slot before the controller is touched and retired on every exit path, and RetryAfter, the moment a refusing controller may be written to again; and the self-fence exposure the arming path now records for this host, which EnsurePoolBootRestriction reads. On the pool master, in its durable PoolMembership: PoolMember.peer_origin, which the master now derives from its configured pool-peer listener rather than from port 9444 and its default route, and PoolMember.SystemUUID, which an ejected row no longer holds against a re-imaged machine. All three already existed as records; only their values and the moments they are written changed, so a fresh Controller recovers them by the unchanged inventory and adoption path - each host re-enrolls, the master reports its membership and each host reports its own local state, and the Controller mirrors what it is told.

verification.method: Runnable checks only; no physical hardware was involved at any point. Each of the twenty-three fixes was reverted in place, its regression check observed failing with the message recorded in its BUG_LEDGER entry, and the fix restored. Go, run from the repository root: go build ./... PASS; go vet ./internal/... ./cmd/... PASS; go test -count=1 ./internal/agent/ ok 11.854s and ok 11.950s on later runs; go test -count=1 ./internal/vmhost/ ok 8.635s; go test -count=1 ./internal/controller/ ok 31.472s; go test -count=1 ./internal/localcore/ ok 8.365s; go test -count=1 -race ./internal/agent/ ok 29.176s; go test -race -count=1 -run 'Hwmon|Hardware|History' ./internal/agent/ ok 1.517s; gofmt clean on every changed file. New or extended regression tests: TestAJoiningHostWithNoAddressYetDoesNotTearThePoolDown, TestLeavingThePoolClusterReleasesItsCorosyncConfiguration, TestIPMIFenceRunsOverTheSameRMCPSessionTheIdentityWasProvedOver, TestATruncatedPassKeepsTheResultsItDidNotReach, TestAPaddedPasswordAPeerOffersIsRefused, TestAnInterruptedProvisioningLeavesNoSecondPasswordFile, TestRemovingTheAccountRetiresThePasswordItOpened, TestAControllerThatKeepsRefusingIsNotRewrittenEveryPass, TestAnEjectedRowDoesNotHoldAMachineIdentityForEver, TestPoolJoinInvitationWorksOutMasterPeerOrigin, TestADisclaimedMasteryStaysInsideThePool, TestHwmonSensorsWithinReturnsLastValuesWhenAChipStalls, TestHwmonBudgetKeepsCPUAndNVMeAheadOfDisks, TestRingFileAtSeriesCapEvictsACoreForATemperature, TestReadHardwareReportsEverySection, TestTheWatchdogProofAndReadinessAgreeThroughTheRealPromotionPath, TestAPromotionFencesByTheMethodReadinessPromised, TestAnArmedMasterIsRestrictedOnTheBootAfterItsWatchdogCouldHaveResetIt, TestAnArmedHostDoesNotReadItsOwnSBDAsAnotherProgram. Web, run from web/: npx tsc --noEmit exit 0 with no diagnostics; node --test src/*.test.mjs tests 11, pass 11, fail 0 - including the new Host-fencing alert source assertion in pool-members.test.mjs and the new all-series contrast assertion in stats.test.mjs. Python: python3 -m unittest tests.test_ci_security tests.test_website_hosting tests.test_release_publish Ran 33 tests OK, covering the two new workflow regressions test_website_release_id_is_left_to_the_deploy_script and test_deploy_checks_and_website_build_run_before_the_tag_moves; python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_repository_privacy.py' OK, 1 test. Documentation: python3 scripts/generate_api.py --check PASS and python3 scripts/check_docs.py --worktree PASS. NOT verified: no physical management controller was contacted, no host was powered off, no physical watchdog was read, armed or expired, no release was published and no package or ISO was built. The fencing measurements these fixes were reviewed against come from a nested virtual laboratory (docs/qa/2026-09-22-automatic-host-fencing.md); the pool-cluster states have no browser capture at all, and the browser review that exists used mocked API replies. The guide steps corrected here have not been walked through against a running pool. Final run on the settled tree after the review round: go build ./..., go vet ./internal/... ./cmd/..., go test -count=1 ./internal/... (11 packages ok), go test -race -count=1 ./internal/agent/ ./internal/vmhost/ ./internal/controller/ ok, gofmt clean on every changed Go file; cd web && npx tsc --noEmit and node --test src/*.test.mjs 11 pass 0 fail; python3 -m unittest discover -s tests OK; python3 scripts/check_docs.py --worktree passed; python3 scripts/generate_api.py --check current. The two transient failures seen while agents edited the same package concurrently were rerun eight times and three times under -race on the settled tree, all passing.
